title: A fresh idempotency key per click means a retry after a lost response refunds twice
evidence: api.js:32 says the key lets the server ignore a repeated request for the same attempt, and README.md:9 says a repeated request does not refund twice. app.js:128 generates a new UUID on every call of refundSelected. On any error (app.js:131-133) the selection in state.selected is kept and the finally block re-enables the button (app.js:135-136, renderRefundButton line 83), so the next click sends the same ids under a different key. Traced; I could not run the app (Bash and browser denied).
failing_case: Select 3 orders, click Refund, confirm. The server processes the refund but the response is lost (proxy 502, timeout, tab offline). The user sees 'The refund was not confirmed...'. The 3 rows are still ticked and the button is enabled. One more click and confirm sends the same ids with a new Idempotency-Key, so the server treats it as a new request and refunds the same customers again. The advice 'Reload and check the order statuses' is text only; nothing enforces it.
remediation: Create the key once per intended refund (the selection) and reuse it on every retry until the server confirms. When the outcome is unknown (network error, 5xx, bad JSON), keep refund disabled until load() has shown the real statuses.

title: A successful refund whose response has no JSON body is reported as 'not confirmed', and the response content is never inspected
evidence: request() is shared by reads and writes. For any res.ok response it requires a JSON body (api.js:16-20) and throws ApiError otherwise. refund() (api.js:33-39) returns that value and app.js:128-129 never looks at it. A POST that answers 201 or 204 with an empty body is a normal REST shape, and the README specifies no response contract. A 200 body that lists per-order failures would also be shown as 'Refunded N orders.' Traced.
failing_case: The proxy answers POST /api/v1/refunds with 204 No Content after refunding. res.json() rejects, so the user sees 'The refund was not confirmed. The server sent a response that is not valid JSON. Reload and check...'. The table is not reloaded (app.js:130 is skipped) and still shows the orders as paid with the boxes ticked. A retry sends a new Idempotency-Key and refunds again.
remediation: Let refund() treat any 2xx as success. Parse the body only if there is one, validate the shape the server promises (for example refunded and failed id lists), and show partial failures per order. Always reload after a refund attempt.

title: No eligibility rule: refunded and pending orders can be selected and sent for refund
evidence: Every row gets a checkbox (app.js:37-45) whatever its status. selectedOrders does not check order.status, renderRefundButton enables on count alone, and domain.js has no 'canRefund' rule although it already models status (domain.js:5, 25). The confirm dialog (app.js:123) then adds the totals of those orders and says 'This sends money back to the customers.'
failing_case: Set Status to 'refunded', tick two rows, click 'Refund 2 orders', confirm. The client posts ids of orders that are already refunded. Only an unspecified server check (README.md:8 covers user permission, not order state) stands between this and paying the customer twice. Pending (unpaid) orders can be sent the same way.

requirement.why: The data model has paid/refunded/pending statuses and revenue treats only 'paid' as money received (domain.js:26); refunding a non-paid order is not meaningful.

remediation: Add a pure canRefund(order) to domain.js with a test, render the checkbox disabled (with a reason) for ineligible orders, and filter in selectedOrders.

title: normaliseOrder turns a missing or non-numeric total into 0 instead of dropping the record
evidence: The header comment on line 7 promises null for 'no numeric total'. Number(null) is 0, Number('') is 0, Number([]) is 0, Number(false) is 0 and Number(true) is 1, all finite, so the guard on line 12 passes. Number(' ') is 0 too. Negative totals also pass. Traced against the ECMAScript conversion rules; not executed.
failing_case: The API returns {id: 7, total: null, customer: {name: 'Ann'}, status: 'paid'}. The row is shown as $0.00 'paid', the 'skipped' warning (app.js:103) never fires, revenue silently omits it, and the user can tick it and refund it; the confirm dialog says 'totalling $0.00' for a real order.
remediation: Accept only typeof raw.total === 'number' or a non-empty numeric string, reject non-finite and negative values, and add tests for null, '', [], true and -5.

quote: const amount = picked.reduce((sum, o) => sum + o.total, 0);
title: Refund amount shown in the confirm dialog is computed in the view and disagrees with the revenue rule in domain.js
evidence: domain.js:25-30 treats the money an order represents as total, less 10% for gold, plus 8.25% tax. app.js:122 sums the raw o.total in a handler with floating-point addition and no tier or tax. The two places encode different ideas of what the customer paid. Arithmetic on money in a handler is the domain-leak row of the code rubric.
failing_case: A gold customer's paid order has total 100.00. The Revenue tile counts $97.43 for it (9000 cents plus 8.25%), while the dialog says 'Refund 1 order totalling $100.00'. One of the two figures is wrong, and the user is asked to approve a money movement on the unlabelled one.

requirement.why: Which figure the customer actually paid is not stated anywhere in the payload; the two code paths disagree.

remediation: Move the amount into one pure, tested function in domain.js (integer cents) that both revenue and the refund confirmation use, and settle with the owner which figure is the refundable amount.

title: After a successful refund, a failed reload leaves the refunded orders selected and refundable
evidence: On success showToast says 'Refunded N orders.' and load() runs (app.js:129-130). load() swallows its own errors (app.js:105-108). Selection is only cleared inside load() after a successful getOrders (app.js:98). On failure state.orders still holds the old rows with status 'paid', state.selected is unchanged, loading goes false in finally (app.js:110), and renderRefundButton (line 83) leaves the button enabled because n > 0.
failing_case: Select an order, refund it successfully. The GET /orders reload then fails (503, offline, session expiry). The page shows the toast 'Refunded 1 order.', an error line, and the old table where the order is still ticked, still 'paid', with 'Refund 1 order' enabled. A second click and confirm sends a second refund for the same order under a new idempotency key.
remediation: Clear state.selected (and mark the refunded ids as pending reconciliation) as soon as refund() resolves, before calling load(). Do not leave stale rows refundable after a write succeeded.

title: Disabling the focused Next, Previous or Refund button drops keyboard focus to the page body
evidence: renderTable sets prev/next disabled (app.js:71-72) right after the click that moved the page. renderRefundButton (app.js:83) disables the refund button while refunding and again when the selection is cleared after the reload (app.js:98). A disabled control cannot keep focus. Traced; the Playwright check could not be run.
failing_case: Keyboard user tabs to Next and presses Enter on the second-to-last page. Next becomes disabled, focus is lost and the next Tab starts again from the top of the document. The same happens on the Refund button as soon as the click disables it, and again after the post-refund reload. The user loses their place and gets no spoken result for the refund.
remediation: Move focus before disabling (to the table caption or a heading on page change, to the status message after a refund), or use aria-disabled and ignore the click instead of the disabled attribute.
